Sure! Here’s a classic roasted chicken recipe that you can scale up for five whole chickens (or adjust if you’re using pieces). I’ll give you a basic outline, ingredient list, and step‑by‑step instructions so you can make it at home or plan a meal for a gathering.

---

## Classic Herb & Lemon Roasted Chicken  
*(Serves about 5–6 people per chicken – perfect for a family dinner or a small party.)*

### Ingredients (for one whole chicken)

| Ingredient | Quantity (per chicken) |
|------------|------------------------|
| Whole chicken (bone‑in, skin‑on) | 1 (about 1.8 kg / 4 lb) |
| Olive oil | 2 Tbsp |
| Salt | 1 tsp (plus extra for seasoning) |
| Freshly ground black pepper | ½ tsp |
| Garlic cloves | 4–6, smashed |
| Fresh rosemary sprigs | 4–6 |
| Fresh thyme sprigs | 4–6 |
| Lemon | 1, halved |
| Onion | 1, quartered |
| Carrots | 2–3, cut into chunks |
| Celery stalks | 2–3, cut into chunks |
| Optional: butter | 2 Tbsp, melted |

> **Tip:** If you’re roasting multiple chickens, keep the seasoning amounts the same per bird; you’ll just multiply the total quantity accordingly.

### Equipment Needed

* Oven (preheated to 425 °F / 220 °C)
* Roasting pan or sheet pan
* Meat thermometer (to check doneness)
* Aluminum foil (optional, for tenting)

---

## Step‑by‑Step Instructions

| Step | Action | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| 1 | Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C). | A hot oven helps crisp the skin. |
| 2 | Prepare the chicken: pat dry with paper towels. | Dry skin yields better browning. |
| 3 | Season inside and out: rub olive oil over the entire surface, then sprinkle salt, pepper, and crushed garlic. | You can also add a pinch of paprika or smoked paprika for color. |
| 4 | Stuff cavity: place lemon halves, onion quarters, and half the rosemary/thyme inside each chicken. | This infuses flavor from the inside. |
| 5 | Tie legs together with kitchen twine (optional but keeps shape). | Tying ensures even cooking. |
| 6 | Arrange vegetables around the chicken in the pan. | These will roast alongside and become a side dish. |
| 7 | Roast uncovered for 20 min, then reduce heat to 375 °F (190 °C) and continue roasting until the internal temperature reaches 165 °F (74 °C) in the thickest part of thigh. | Total time ≈ 1 h 30 min–1 h 45 min depending on size. |
| 8 | Baste occasionally with melted butter or pan juices. | Adds richness and helps brown the skin. |
| 9 | Tent with foil if the skin starts to burn before the meat is done. | Keep an eye on it—don’t let it get too dark. |
|10 | Rest: remove from oven, tent loosely with foil, and rest for 15 min before carving. | Resting allows juices to redistribute. |
|11 | Serve: carve and serve with roasted veggies, mashed potatoes, or a fresh salad. | Pair with a light white wine or sparkling water. |

---

## Scaling Up for Five Chickens

| Item | Amount for 5 chickens |
|------|-----------------------|
| Whole chickens | 5 (≈ 9 kg / 20 lb total) |
| Olive oil | 10 Tbsp (≈ ⅔ cup) |
| Salt | 5 tsp + extra for seasoning |
| Black pepper | 2 ½ tsp |
| Garlic cloves | 20–25 |
| Rosemary sprigs | 20–25 |
| Thyme sprigs | 20–25 |
| Lemons | 5 |
| Onions | 5 |
| Carrots | 10–12 |
| Celery | 10–12 |
| Butter | 10 Tbsp (≈ ⅓ cup) |

> **Cooking Tip:** If your oven can’t hold all five at once, roast them in batches or use two pans simultaneously. Make sure each batch gets enough space for air circulation.

---

## Quick Time Calculator (Optional)

If you’d like to estimate cooking time based on weight, here’s a simple rule of thumb:

**Rule:** *Add 15 minutes per pound (0.45 kg) after the initial 20 minute “blow‑off” period.*

So for a 4 lb chicken:
```
Initial high‑temp phase: 20 min
Remaining time: 15 min × 4 lb = 60 min
Total: 80 min (≈ 1 h 20 min)
```

Feel free to tweak the seasonings or add other aromatics (e.g., bay leaves, orange zest, or a splash of white wine) to suit your taste. Enjoy your cooking adventure!
